symptoms: Stunting of plants Ringspots and mottling on leaves and fruit Chlorotic blotches and line patterns on leaves Wilting and purpling of leaves Necrotic lesions on stems Distorted or necrotic fruits
management: prevention: Use virus- and thrips-free transplants Remove infected plants and old crops Maintain weed-free buffers of at least 25 m Sanitation practices in greenhouses and fields resistant_varieties: Use TSWV-resistant capsicum and tomato varieties Consider resistance-breaking strains and maintain hygiene chemical_control: Limited value of insecticides against vectors due to rapid resistance Insecticides may reduce thrips populations but do not eliminate virus spread biological_control: Predators of thrips such as Orius insidiosus (minute pirate bugs) and Geocoris punctipes (big-eyed bugs)
